paper_title: Upper Limit on the QCD Axion Mass from Isolated Neutron Star Cooling
suggested_experiment_name: Neutron Star Cooling Constraint on QCD Axion Mass (Magnificent Seven + PSR J0659)
coupling_convention: m_a in eV (axion mass on y-axis); x-axis is tan(β) which controls the relative coupling of the axion to neutrons and protons in the DFSZ model. The plot shows the upper limit on axion mass as a function of tan(β).
notes: Paper constrains QCD axion mass m_a ≲ 16 meV at 95% confidence within the KSVZ model by comparing NS cooling simulations with observed luminosity and kinematic age data from five isolated neutron stars (four Magnificent Seven NSs plus PSR J0659). This is a mass-independent bound valid over a wide range since the constraint arises from cooling physics rather than a specific mass-dependent resonance. The limit is derived from the requirement that axion energy losses do not exceed observed cooling rates. For DFSZ model, limits depend on tan β (shown in Fig. 3). The paper also reports |g_an| < 1.3×10^-9 and |g_ap| < 1.5×10^-9 at 95% CL for axion-neutron and axion-proton couplings respectively. The primary result is on the axion mass itself (not a coupling constant on the y-axis), making AxionMass the appropriate coupling type.
